audience.programmeDescription: Biomedical Sciences at Leiden studies the healthy and diseased human body, from molecules and cells to organ systems and clinical research. It combines biological mechanisms, laboratory work, quantitative research methods and scientific communication.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A complete UCR comparison is awaiting clarification of a Leiden course-entry requirement. The published curriculum allocation is shown below, including the 19-EC research project and 30 EC of elective study. Relevant UCR biomedical, population-health and quantitative options have been identified, but their comparison cannot yet be finalised.

curriculum.limitation: The published allocation totals 180 EC: 60 EC in each of the first two years and 30 EC of compulsory study plus 30 EC of choice in year three. This is not yet a fully verified degree pathway: Human Pathology requires Physiology Advanced Concepts, which is absent from the current programme. Its applicable replacement or removal still needs confirmation.

componentNotes.lei-y1-bast: The 5 EC belong to the assessed year assignment. BAST themes embedded in other modules carry no additional separate credits.
componentNotes.lei-y2-pathology: Published entry conditions include Human Biology, Biomolecules, Cellular Communication, Medical Genetics, Immunology, Physiology Basic Concepts and Physiology Advanced Concepts. The last prerequisite is absent from the current programme; its applicable replacement or removal remains unresolved.
componentNotes.lei-y3-oncology: Required module after completed Molecular Biology, Cellular Communication and Immunology.
componentNotes.lei-y3-srp: Required individual supervised biomedical research. All first- and second-year examinations must be passed. Written project agreement must reach the internship committee at least four weeks before the start.
componentNotes.lei-y3-cis: Required scientific writing, peer review and research poster; Communication in Science 1 and 2 must be completed.
componentNotes.lei-y3-electives: 30 EC of choice from 2026–2027. Possibilities include a full minor, a half-minor with electives or a project extension, or a separate elective research project. Minor availability and registration conditions apply. An elective research project must differ from the compulsory project in subject, techniques and department.
